'''Sydney Leach FRS''' (11 April 1924 – 24 December 2019) was a British scientist based in France whose research areas included the fields of [[spectroscopy]], photophysics and [[photochemistry]]. His work studying molecular ions led to new areas of interest, including [[Planetary science|planetary]] and [[atmospheric science]], as well as the newly developing field of [[astrobiology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celebrating Sydney Leach: From Molecular Photophysics to Astrobiology – with Musical Interludes - Sciencesconf.org|url=https://astromolecleach.sciencesconf.org/|access-date=2021-12-01|website=astromolecleach.sciencesconf.org}}</ref>

His scientific career was based in Paris, including his founding Directorship at Laboratoire de Photophysique Moléculaire Orsay, and his later move to L'Observatoire de Meudon where he was based for the remainder of his career.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Astronomical Union {{!}} IAU|url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/7868/|access-date=2021-12-01|website=www.iau.org}}</ref>

Leach was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Field|first1=D.|last2=Simons|first2=J. P.|last3=Cockell|first3=C.|date=2020|title=Sydney Leach. 11 April 1924—24 December 2019|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=69|pages=313–332|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0018|s2cid=221714840|doi-access=free}}</ref>
